sentences.text:
This appeal by the appellant/claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 06.12.2021 passed by Third Additional Member, MACT, Sagar in MACC No.396/2018, whereby appellant's claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act has been dismissed.
2.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has not properly appreciated the deposition of Kamal Yadav (PW/2), from whose deposition accident is clearly established.

Further,
it is also urged that FIR Ex.P/2 has been lodged immediately after the accident, wherein number of offending vehicle along with name of driver is mentioned.
It is also established from evidence on record that offending vehicle was wrongly parked on the road without there being any parking lights on.
The Tribunal has not properly appreciated facts mentioned in the FIR Ex.P/2.
On above grounds, it is urged that Tribunal has wrongly dismissed the claim of appellant.

Hence,
compensation be awarded.

3. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the appellant's witness Kamal Yadav has made contradictory statement, in his deposition and his statement is also contrary to what is mentioned in FIR Ex.P/2.
It is also urged that appellant was sitting on the fuel tank of motor cycle and three persons were sitting on the motor cycle at the time of accident.
After referring to the deposition of Kamal Yadav (PW/2), the Tribunal has rightly dismissed appellant's claim.
No interference is required in the same.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case.

5. In FIR Ex.P/2, which has been lodged by the sister of appellant immediately after the accident, it is mentioned that the driver of offending vehicle had parked the truck wrongly on the road,
therefore, motorcycle collided with the truck.

Contrary to what is mentioned in the FIR Ex.P/2,
appellant's witness Kamal Yadav (PW/2) has stated that the accident occurred because driver of offending vehicle applied brake all of a sudden and on account of which motor cycle collided with the truck.
But this witness in his cross-examination has admitted that it is correct that the truck was inside the white line of the road and it was not on the road.
The driver of offending vehicle has just applied brake to stop the vehicle.

It is correct that at the time of accident, he was inside the Dhaba,
therefore, he cannot tell as to on account of whose negligence accident occurred.
6. It is also evident from the record of the case that accident had occurred at about 4.30 P.M. during day time.

It is also evident from deposition of Kamal Yadav (PW/2) that at the time of accident, the person riding the motorcycle has covered his face with towel and two children were sitting on the motorcycle.
7. Hence, in view of the discussion in foregoing paras, it cannot be said that the Tribunal has wrongly dismissed the claim of appellant.
Hence, no interference is required in the findings recorded by the Tribunal.
8. The appeal filed by the appellant is dismissed.
